# Entire CLI

Entire hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written in your repo.

With Entire, you can:

  * Understand why code changed — see the full prompt/response transcript and files touched
  * Recover instantly — rewind to a known-good checkpoint when an agent goes sideways and resume seamlessly
  * Keep Git history clean — preserve agent context on a separate branch
  * Onboard faster — show the path from prompt → change → commit
  * Maintain traceability — support audit and compliance requirements when needed

## Why Entire

  * Understand why code changed, not just what — Transcripts, prompts, files touched, token usage, tool calls, and more are captured alongside every commit.
  * Rewind and resume from any checkpoint — Go back to any previous agent session and pick up exactly where you or a coworker left off.
  * Full context preserved and searchable — A versioned record of every AI interaction tied to your git history, with nothing lost.
  * Zero context switching — Git-native, two-step setup, works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, and more.

## Table of Contents

  * Why Entire
  * Quick Start
  * Typical Workflow
  * Key Concepts
    * How It Works
    * Strategy
  * Local Device Auth Testing
  * Commands Reference
  * Configuration
  * Security & Privacy
  * Troubleshooting
  * Development
  * Getting Help
  * License

## Requirements

  * Git
  * macOS, Linux or Windows
  * Supported agent installed and authenticated

## Quick Start
    
    # Install stable via Homebrew
    brew tap entireio/tap
    brew install --cask entire
    
    # Or install nightly via Homebrew
    brew tap entireio/tap
    brew install --cask entire@nightly
    
    # Or install stable via install.sh
    curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
    
    # Or install nightly via install.sh
    curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
    
    # Or install stable via Scoop (Windows)
    scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
    scoop install entire/cli
    
    # Or install via Go (development/manual setup)
    go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
    
    # Linux: Add Go binaries to PATH (add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if not already configured)
    export PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
    
    # Enable in your project
    cd your-project && entire enable
    
    # Check status
    entire status

After the initial setup, use `entire agent` to add or remove agents, `entire configure` to update non-agent settings, and `entire enable` / `entire disable` to toggle Entire on or off.

## Release Channels

Entire currently ships two release channels:

  * `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
  * `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.

How to use each channel:

  * Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
  * Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
  * `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
  * `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
  * Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/cli`

## Typical Workflow

### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
    
    `entire enable
    `

On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install. 
Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:

Agent  | Hook Location  | Format
--- | --- | ---
Claude Code  | `.claude/settings.json`  | JSON hooks config
Codex  | `.codex/hooks.json`  | JSON hooks config

# CHANGELOG.md


# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-07-27

### Added

  * `entire doctor migrate-checkpoints` migrates existing checkpoints from the git-branch backend to git-refs (#1611)
  * git-refs checkpoints can be discovered on a second device via remote enumeration, and `entire checkpoint list --json` gives a machine-readable listing (migrate off `rewind --list`) (#1771, #1768)
  * Hidden `entire checkpoint resume` command (#1701)
  * `entire explain` streams live progress and reports an observable-state timeout diagnostic (#964)
  * `entire review`: live token counts for the Claude and Codex reviewers, and Codex now runs real skills via on-disk `$name` discovery and native invocation (#1666, #1669)
  * Import gains imported sessions in `entire session list`, anchors imported checkpoints to the default-branch head, and warns when importing agent history while logged out (#1699, #1825, #1774)
## [0.8.0] - 2026-07-06

### Added

  * A git-refs checkpoint store (per-checkpoint git-ref backend) with ULID checkpoint IDs, ID-kind read routing across git backends, and pre-push push progress (#1566, #1629, #1630, #1632)
  * `entire agent-help`: machine-readable, agent-facing usage rendered live from the Cobra command tree, plus active and passive discovery paths so no-channel agents (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, MCP hosts) can reach it via `entire help`, the `status` footer, `status --json`, and an MCP tool (#1562, #1585)
  * `entire experts` (hidden, via `entire labs`): ranks prior agent sessions with real evidence for a given path — matching checkpoints, attributed lines, skills, tools, and MCP servers — without exposing prompts or transcripts, routed to the repo's entire-api cell with an identity token (#1573, #1588)
  * `entire api`, a `gh api`-style authenticated passthrough that dials the control-plane core (default) or your home entire-api cell (`--to cell`) with the right bearer, filling `{owner}`/`{repo}`/`{repo_id}` placeholders from the current repo (#1605)
  * `git-remote-entire` now stamps a versioned `User-Agent` (`git-remote-entire/<version>`) on every outbound HTTP request, so the helper is identifiable in upstream access logs (#1348)
  * `entire repo mirror create` skips clone polling when the upstream has no refs, printing a short note and returning instead of waiting out the timeout (#1357)
  * `entire repo mirror create` now explains suspended mirrors with resume guidance instead of a generic error (#1344)
  * Better alignment of the labs commands (#1345)
  * Minor cosmetic tweaks to command output (#1343)

### Housekeeping

  * Auth review follow-ups and a keyring-safe `cli` `TestMain` (#1360)
  * Made the `GitTerminalPromptOnIsNotAgent` test hermetic (#1361)
  * Dependency bumps: `actions/checkout`, `github/codeql-action`, and the Go dependencies group (#1338, #1339, #1340)

## [0.7.3] - 2026-06-02

### Fixed

  * Fixed a bug where internal API calls didn't follow a redirect properly (#1327)

## [0.7.2] - 2026-06-02

### Fixed

  * macOS release binaries are Developer ID signed and notarized again. Adding the `git-remote-entire` binary in 0.7.0 gave the release builds explicit ids that no longer matched the notarization step's default filter, so 0.7.0 shipped ad-hoc-signed binaries that macOS Gatekeeper refused to run — surfacing as Homebrew shell-completion errors and `killed` on launch (#1324)

### Housekeeping

  * The release workflow now fails closed when any macOS binary is not Developer ID signed, so an un-notarized build can no longer ship silently (#1324)

  * `entire labs review` command — runs configured review skills inside an agent session, with single- and multi-agent picker flows, a Bubble Tea live dashboard, an optional cross-agent synthesis verdict, and `entire review attach` for post-hoc tagging. Reviews are recorded in checkpoint metadata so future commits know the code was reviewed (#993, #1105, #1106, #1107, #1111, #1112)
  * `entire recap` command, with an interactive TUI for browsing recaps (#1015, #1113)
  * kubectl-style external command resolution: `entire <name>` falls through to `entire-<name>` on PATH (#1104)
  * Managed plugin install directory and `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` for plugin discovery (#1121)

### Changed

  * Checkpoint commit signing now uses go-git's program signer for custom signing setups (#1128)
  * Checkpoints v2 (work in progress): dual-write to v1 and v2 during the transition; migration speedups via fast-path checks and rerun de-duplication; clearer completion message after the progress bar (#1108, #1109, #1110, #1114)
## [0.6.0] - 2026-05-04

### Added

  * Detection of pushes to protected branches, with a clearer warning before the push proceeds (#1033)
  * Improved auth token management in the CLI (#1050)
  * `entire explain --generate` now supports external agents for summary generation (#1044)
  * `entire search` TUI gains a unified palette with the activity view, markdown snippet rendering, and shell completions (#1053)
  * Homebrew now prompts users to update when a new version is released, and Homebrew cask completions are generated at install time (#1057, #1085)
  * Nested perf spans render in traces for richer debugging (#1073)

### Changed

  * CLI restructured around `session` / `checkpoint` / `agent` / `auth` / `doctor` command groups (#1062)
  * Charm TUI stack upgraded to v2; dispatch repo links added to the dispatch wizard (#1048)
  * TUI navigation help aligned across `entire activity` and `entire search` (#1058, #1064)

## [0.5.4] - 2026-04-10

### Added

  * Checkpoints v2 (work in progress): v2-aware `explain` with compact transcript support, push logic for v2 refs, compact transcript format for Factory AI Droid, Codex, and Copilot CLI, and `entire migrate-v2` migration command (#864, #821, #852, #862, #891)
  * `entire search` command is now available, with improved TUI usability and managed search subagents (#907, #856, #833)
  * Stale session indicator in `entire status` output (#853)
  * `entire status` now shows active agents (#847)
  * `entire configure --remove-agent` to remove agent configurations (#851)
  * Codex support for `explain --generate` with summary timeout (#875, #876)
  * Nightly releases via GoReleaser and Homebrew tap, with `install.sh` nightly support (#825, #911)
  * Hook overwrite detection during running agent prompts (#791)

### Housekeeping

  * Factory AI Droid added to all documentation (#655)
  * Copilot CLI added to all documentation (#653)
  * Updated Discord release message to include installation link (#646)
  * Dependency bumps: actions/create-github-app-token 3.0.0, jdx/mise-action 4, gitleaks 8.30.1 (#706, #694, #689)
  * Added tests for git remote related flows (#696)
  * "Why Entire" section in README (#331)

### Thanks

Thanks to @mvanhorn for multiple contributions including hk hook manager detection, bare repo worktree ID fix, rewind subdirectory path fix, and mise install detection!

## [0.5.0] - 2026-03-06

### Added

  * External agent plugin system with lazy discovery, timeout protection, feature-flag gating, and stdin/stdout caps (docs, #604)
  * Vogon deterministic fake agent for cost-free E2E canary testing (#619)
  * `entire resume` now supports squash-merged commits by parsing checkpoint IDs from the metadata branch (#534, #602, #593)
## [0.4.9] - 2026-03-02

### Added

  * Factory AI Droid agent integration with full checkpoint, resume, rewind, and session transcript support (#435, #552)
  * `--absolute-git-hook-path` flag for `entire enable` to set up git hooks with absolute paths to the entire binary (#495)
  * Architecture tests enforcing agent package boundaries (#569)

### Changed

  * Improved TTY handling consolidated into a single location (#543)
  * Simplified PATH setup message in install script (#566)
  * Skip version check for dev builds instead of all prereleases (#401)
  * Skip fully-condensed ENDED sessions in PostCommit to avoid redundant work (#556, #568)
  * Don't update LastInteraction when only git hooks were triggered (#550)

### Fixed

  * `entire explain` hanging on repos with many checkpoints (#551)
  * `prepare-commit-msg` hook performance for large repos (#553)
  * Don't wait for sessions older than 120s during transcript flush (#545)

  * First commit in the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch is now trying to lookup author info from local and global git config (#262)

  * "Reference not found" error when enabling Entire in an empty repository (#255)
  * Deleted files in task checkpoints are now correctly computed (#218)

  * Fixed incorrect resume documentation (#224)

L73: Install the Entire CLI on your system
L74: 
L75: Copy page Copy page
L76: 
L77: ##
L78: 
L79: cite17†​ L80: 
L81: System Requirements
L82: 
L83:   * Operating System: macOS, Linux, Windows
L84:   * Git: Version 2.25 or later
L85:   * Shell: Bash or Zsh (for hook installation)
L86: ##
L87: 
L88: cite18†​ L89: 
L90: Installation Methods
L91: 
L92: Entire currently ships two release channels:
L93: 
L94:   * `stable`: recommended for most users. This is the default channel for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
L95:   * `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier.
L96: Entire uses Homebrew casks so the CLI can be installed from the same signed release artifacts used by other install methods.
L97: 
L98:   * macOS (Homebrew)
L99: 
L100:   * Linux
L101: 
L102:   * Windows (Scoop)
L103: 
L104:   * From Source
L105: The easiest way to install on macOS is via Homebrew.First, tap and trust the Entire tap. This is a one-time setup:
L106: 
L107:     `brew tap entireio/tap
L108:     brew trust entireio/tap
L109:     `
L110: 
L111: Homebrew 5.2.0 and 6.0.0 and later require trusting a third-party tap with `brew trust` before installing its casks. See cite23†Tap Trust†docs.brew.sh .
L112: 
L113: Then install the stable channel:
L114: 
L115:     `brew install --cask entire
L116:     `
L117: 
L118: Or install the nightly channel:
L119: 
L120:     `brew install --cask entire@nightly
L121:     `
L122: To upgrade the stable channel:
L123: 
L124:     `brew upgrade --cask entire
L125:     `
L126: 
L127: To upgrade the nightly channel:
L128: 
L129:     `brew upgrade --cask entire@nightly
L130:     `
L131: 
L132: Use the install script for Linux.Stable is the default:
L133: 
L134:     `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
L135:     `
L136: 
L137: To install the nightly channel:
L138: 
L139:     `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
L140:     `
L141: Or download the binary directly:
L142: 
L143:     `# Download the latest release
L144:     curl -LO https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire-linux-amd64.tar.gz
L145: 
L146:     # Extract and install
L147:     tar -xzf entire-linux-amd64.tar.gz
L148:     sudo mv entire /usr/local/bin/
L149:     `
L150: 
L151: For ARM64 systems:
L152: 
L153:     `curl -LO https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire-linux-arm64.tar.gz
L154:     `
L155: Scoop currently supports the stable channel only:
L156: 
L157:     `scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
L158:     scoop install entire/cli
L159:     `
L160: 
L161: To update:
L162: 
L163:     `scoop update entire/cli
L164:     `
L165: 
L166: If you have Go 1.21+ installed, you can build from source:
L167: 
L168:     `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest
L169:     `
L170: Or clone and build manually:
L171: 
L172:     `git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
L173:     cd cli
L174:     go build -o entire ./cmd/entire
L175:     sudo mv entire /usr/local/bin/
L176:     `
L177: ##
L178: 
L179: cite19†​ L180: 
L181: Verify Installation
L182: 
L183: After installation, verify that Entire is working:
L184: 
L185:     `entire version
L186:     `
L187: 
L188: You should see output like:
L189: 
L190:     `entire version 1.0.0 (abc1234)
L191:     `
L192: 
L193: The `entire` binary needs to be on your `$PATH` for agent hooks and Git hooks to work.
L194: 
L195: ##
L196: 
L197: cite20†​ L198: 
L199: Shell Completion
L200: 
L201: Entire supports shell completion for Bash and Zsh.
L202: 
L203:   * Bash
L204: 
L205:   * Zsh
L206: 
L207: Add to your `~/.bashrc`:
L208: 
L209:     `source <(entire completion bash)
L210:     `
L211: ##
L212: 
L213: cite21†​ L214: 
L215: Uninstalling
L216: 
L217:   * Homebrew
L218: 
L219:   * Manual
L220: 
L221:     `brew uninstall --cask entire
L222:     `
L223:

L225:     `
L226: 
L227: Also remove any configuration:
L228: 
L229:     `rm -rf ~/.config/entire
L230:     `

L73: # Quickstart
L74: 
L75: Get started with Entire by creating your first checkpoint.
L76: 
L77: Copy page Copy page
L78: 
L79: This quickstart walks you from installing Entire to creating your first checkpoint: a record of the prompts, transcript, tool calls, and file changes behind an AI-assisted commit.
L80: ##
L81: 
L82: cite17†​ L83: 
L84: Prerequisites
L85: 
L86:   * Git installed and configured
L87:   * An AI coding agent installed, such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Factory, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Pi
L88:   * macOS, Linux, or Windows
L89:   * Optional: GitHub CLI (`gh`) installed and authenticated, if you want Entire to create and push a private GitHub repository during setup
L90: ##
L91: 
L92: cite18†​ L93: 
L94: 1. Install Entire
L95: 
L96: Entire ships two release channels:
L97: 
L98:   * `stable`: recommended for most users.
L99:   * `nightly`: prerelease builds with newer changes.
L100: Nightly is available through Homebrew and the Linux install script. Scoop currently supports stable only.
L101: 
L102:   * macOS (Homebrew)
L103: 
L104:   * Linux
L105: 
L106:   * Windows (Scoop)
L107:   * From Source
L108: 
L109:     `# One-time setup: tap and trust
L110:     brew tap entireio/tap
L111:     brew trust entireio/tap
L112: 
L113:     # Stable
L114:     brew install --cask entire
L115: 
L116:     # Nightly
L117:     brew install --cask entire@nightly
L118:     `
L119: 
L120:     `# Stable
L121:     curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
L122: 
L123:     # Nightly
L124:     curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
L125:     `
L126: 
L127:     `scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git
L128:     scoop install entire/cli
L129:     `
L130: Verify the installation:
L131: 
L132:     `entire version
L133:     `
L134: ##
L135: 
L136: cite19†​ L137: 
L138: 2. Create a Demo Project
L139: 
L140:     `mkdir entire-demo
L141:     cd entire-demo
L142:     `
L143: 
L144: Already in a Git repository? Skip this step and run the remaining commands from the repository root.
L145: ##
L146: 
L147: cite20†​ L148: 
L149: 3. Enable Entire
L150: 
L151: Choose the agent you already use, then run its setup command.
L152: 
L153: Claude Code

L155:     `entire enable -y --agent claude-code
L156:     `
L157: 
L158: Codex
L159:

L161:     `
L162: 
L163: Copilot CLI
L164: 
L165:     `entire enable -y --agent copilot-cli
L166:     `

L171:     `
L172: 
L173: Factory
L174: 
L175:     `entire enable -y --agent factoryai-droid
L176:     `
L177: 
L178: Gemini CLI
L179: 
L180:     `entire enable -y --agent gemini
L181:     `
L182: OpenCode
L183: 
L184:     `entire enable -y --agent opencode
L185:     `
L186: 
L187: Pi
L188: 
L189:     `entire enable -y --agent pi
L190:     `
L191: 
L192: This installs Git hooks that capture checkpoints when you commit and installs hook configuration for your selected agent. It also creates a `.entire/` directory for project and local settings. For shared projects, commit `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/.gitignore`. Keep `.entire/settings.local.json` local for personal overrides.
L193: Because this starts in a new folder, `entire enable -y` initializes Git and creates an initial commit. If `gh` is installed and authenticated, Entire can also create a private GitHub repository and push the initial commit.
L194: ##
L195: 
L196: cite21†​ L197: 
L198: 4. Start an Agent Session
L199: 
L200: Start the same agent you enabled:
L201: 
L202: Claude Code
L203: 
L204:     `claude
L205:     `
L206: 
L207: Codex
L208: 
L209:     `codex
L210:     `
L211: 
L212: Copilot CLI
L213: 
L214:     `copilot
L215:     `
L216: 
L217: Cursor
L218: 
L219:     `cursor
L220:     `
L221: 
L222: Factory
L223: 
L224:     `droid
L225:     `
L226: 
L227: Gemini CLI
L228: 
L229:     `gemini
L230:     `
L231: 
L232: OpenCode
L233: 
L234:     `opencode
L235:     `
L236: 
L237: Pi
L238: 
L239:     `pi
L240:     `
L241: 
L242: Prompt it to make a small change:
L243: 
L244:     `Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note explaining that this repo is my first Entire checkpoint demo.
L245:     `
L246: When the agent finishes, exit the agent session if needed.
L247: ##
L248: 
L249: cite22†​ L250: 
L251: 5. Commit the Change
L252: 
L253: Check what changed:
L254: 
L255:     `git status
L256:     `
L257: 
L258: Then commit it:
L259: 
L260:     `git add hello-entire.md
L261:     git commit -m "Add first Entire demo file"
L262:     `
L263: Because Entire detected recent agent work, it may ask whether to link this commit to the session context. The agent name will match the integration you enabled:
L264: 
L265:     `Entire: Active <agent> session detected
L266:       Last prompt: Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note...
L267: 
L268:     Link this commit to session context?
L269:       [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice):
L270:     `
L271: 
L272: Press `Enter` or type `y` to link the commit. After the commit succeeds, you have created your first checkpoint.
L273: If you choose `always`, Entire remembers that preference and links future matching commits automatically.
L274: ##
L275: 
L276: cite23†​ L277: 
L278: 6. View Your First Checkpoint
L279: 
L280:     `entire checkpoint list
L281:     `
L282: 
L283: You should see the checkpoint linked to your commit. Entire stores permanent checkpoint data on a Git branch named:
L284: 
L285:     `entire/checkpoints/v1
L286:     `
L287: 
L288: Your working branch stays clean. Entire does not add extra commits to it.
L289: ##
L290: 
L291: cite24†​ L292: 
L293: 7. Optional: Push Your Code and Checkpoint
L294: 
L295: If your repository has a remote, push your code:
L296: 
L297:     `git push
L298:     `
L299: 
L300: Entire’s pre-push hook also syncs checkpoint data to `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
L301: 
L302: Checkpoint data can include session context. If your repository is public, pushed checkpoint history is public too. See cite13†Security & Privacy and cite26†Checkpoint Remote .

L168: ### Added
L169:   * `entire plugin` gains remote install, index discovery, and plugin dependencies — install a plugin by name, URL, or path from any git host, without cloning (cite78†#1422 )
L170:   * `entire repo mirror use` repoints the current clone's git remote at a mirror, closing the last manual step in mirror onboarding (cite79†#1875 )
L171:   * `entire checkpoint explain --repo <owner/name>` explains a checkpoint owned by another repository, reading it from that repo's entire-api cell over HTTP — the drill-down for a cross-repo `search` hit (cite80†#1942 )
L172:   * `entire search --compact` emits a token-lean JSON shape for agents: per hit only identifiers, metadata, and a truncated title snippet, never the full prompt (cite81†#1908 )
L173:   * `entire review --target` reviews a branch, trail ID, or trail URL you are not on, checked out in an isolated worktree (cite82†#1921 )
L174:   * `entire enable` shows live progress while importing existing agent sessions (cite83†#1868 , cite84†#1867 )
L175:   * Repositories using git's reftable ref backend now work; previously `entire enable` and every capture operation aborted with `unknown extension: refstorage` (cite85†#1723 )
L176:   * `entire-ci` is registered as an official plugin, discovered as `entire ci` on PATH (cite86†#1791 )
L177: ### Changed
L178:   * Long-deprecated commands are removed: `entire reset` (use `entire clean`), `entire rewind` and `entire checkpoint rewind`, and the hidden top-level `resume` / `attach` / `explain` / `trace` shortcuts (use the `session`, `checkpoint`, and `doctor` subcommands) (cite87†#1747 )
L179:   * Checkpoints now sync to a single elected remote instead of every remote you push to, and `entire status` names the destination. In a repo with several remotes, pushing anywhere previously copied session transcripts there (cite88†#1893 , cite89†#1905 , cite90†#1898 )
L180:   * `entire search` is promoted out of the experimental gate and is now the canonical spelling across the first-turn injection, the managed search skill, and `agent-help`; `entire checkpoint search` remains as an alias (cite91†#1963 )
L181:   * Code search is generally available: `entire search --code` and the TUI's Code tab no longer require `ENTIRE_CODE_SEARCH=1`, so stable builds stop advertising a flag that refused to run (cite92†#1975 )
L182:   * `entire enable` no longer asks new users to pick a checkpoint backend — git-refs is written silently on first run, and `--checkpoint-backend branch` still selects the branch backend non-interactively (cite93†#1900 )
L183:   * entire-api cell calls and git smart-HTTP traffic authenticate with login JWTs directly, dropping the jurisdiction-token exchange (cite94†#1895 )
L184:   * `entire agent-help` groups commands by who should initiate them, and the first-turn context injection is trimmed to the invariants that hold on every turn (cite95†#1967 )
L185: ### Fixed
L186:   * Agent hook latency: `UserPromptSubmit` no longer blocks on the session lock, and go-git's worktree status no longer walks ignored directories on every hook (cite96†#1880 , cite97†#1911 , cite98†#1968 )
L187:   * Git hooks no longer prompt when a full-screen TUI git client (lazygit, gitui, tig) owns the terminal (cite99†#1907 )
L188:   * A captured file path containing a `.git` component no longer fails the whole checkpoint at tree-encode time (cite100†#1863 )
L189:   * Subagents: resolve transcripts in Claude Code's current layout, carry subagent tokens through to committed checkpoints, skip the task checkpoint when the subagent already committed, and stop Pi's nested subagent processes from claiming the parent session (cite101†#1935 , cite102†#1938 , cite103†#1950 , cite104†#1936 )
L190:   * Checkpoint storage: route backfill writes to the store holding the checkpoint, fetch a locally-missing ref before declaring a backfill target absent, classify a remoteless repo as ref absence rather than an outage, and fall back to the v1-branch store when no checkpoint remote is configured (cite105†#1811 , cite106†#1824 , cite107†#1886 , cite108†#1888 )
L191:   * Hook-config drift is detected for every agent, not just Claude Code, so a committed `.pi` or `.opencode` extension no longer blocks `entire agent add` (cite109†#1939 )
L192:   * Codex: sanitize transcripts before redaction and keep them line-aligned, stop writing `.codex/config.toml` (hooks are on by default), and close the tailer emitted-flag race that made token counts flap (cite110†#1901 , cite111†#1760 , cite112†#1865 )
L193:   * Redaction preserves thinking-block signatures, fixing a 400 on replay (cite113†#1866 )
L194:   * `entire enable` stops the history import on Ctrl-C, and no longer runs it under `--yes` (cite114†#1925 )
L195:   * `entire logout` deletes cached jurisdiction tokens (cite115†#1869 )
L196:   * `entire search` reports an unmatched repo filter as a repo-filter miss instead of a missing region (cite116†#1944 )
L197:   * External command discovery consults the caller's context when resolving a named agent (cite117†#1906 )

item.stdout:
Resolve symbols named by a failing build or test

Usage:
  entire graph explain --repo . [--profile full] [--format text|json|agent] [--max-symbols 8] [--max-context-bytes 2048]

Reads failing build or test output from stdin, passes that output through by default, and appends declarations for the symbols named by the failure. It queries the working tree by default so the declarations match the code that just failed. The command is local and deterministic; it does not call a model or network service.

Flags:
  --repo <path>              Repository (default: current repo)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                             Parsing depth (default: full)
  --cache-dir <path>         Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --format text|json|agent   Output format for resolved declarations (default: text)
  --head                     Resolve declarations from HEAD instead of the working tree
  --worktree                 Resolve declarations from the working tree (default)
  --no-cache                 Disable the committed-tree cache
  --no-echo                  Do not pass the input build output through before declarations
  --max-symbols <n>          Maximum distinct symbol names to resolve (default: 8)
  --max-context-bytes <n>    Byte budget for the declaration block (default: 2048)
  --ignore-file <path>       Extra gitignore-style exclude rules (repeatable)
  --include-file <path>      Re-include ignored paths (gitignore-style; not an allowlist)

Examples:
  go test ./internal/configs -run '^TestX$' 2>&1 | entire graph explain --repo .

item.stdout:
What a name IS: declaration, fields, and method surface

Usage:
  entire graph def NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--members 15] [--format text|json]

Structural declaration lookup: what a name is and, for a type, its fields and associated-function/method surface, drawn from the graph's own membership edges (inherent impl blocks, receiver methods, extension members, partial parts, one hop of trait/module/base acquisition). It reports a method's owning type, and for a trait/interface it reports who implements it. Membership is never inferred from a name resembling another name.

Arguments:
  NAME|<file>:<line>   Symbol name, or a file:line selector

Flags:
  --repo <path>             Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>             Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>             Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --members <n>             Max members listed per group (default: 15)
  --format text|json        Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Total text budget (default: 4096)
  --head                    Query the committed tree (cached)

Examples:
  entire graph def Result --repo .

item.stdout:
Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)

Usage:
  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--relation CALLS] [--direction both|in|out] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 20]

Direct incoming/outgoing relations for one symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at --depth 2. Use it when you want one specific relation/direction; for the full blast radius of a change, prefer impact.

Select a definition with --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME plus --file/--line/--kind when a name is ambiguous. The ambiguity error prints the exact selector for each definition it found.

Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                             Symbol to inspect (required)
  --repo <path>              Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>              Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                 Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>              Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --relation <CALLS>         Relation family to follow (default: CALLS)
  --direction both|in|out    in = callers, out = callees (default: both)
  --depth 1|2                Hops to traverse (default: 1)
  --limit <n>                Max neighbors per direction (default: 20)
  --format json|text|agent   Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>    Output byte budget for agent format (default: 16384)
  --internal-only            Drop unresolved external endpoints
  --exclude-tests            Drop test-only neighbors
  --head                     Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                             Parsing depth (default: full)

Examples:
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --relation CALLS --direction in
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --direction out --depth 2

One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol

Usage:
  entire graph impact --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--depth 1|2] [--limit 15] [--format text|json]

Everything the graph knows about changing one symbol in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth <=2), callees, type consumers (USES_TYPE/PARAM_TYPE/RETURNS_TYPE), data flows, files that historically co-change with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Run this before changing a function/type's behavior.

Ambiguous names return the definition list; rerun with --file/--line/--kind (or --symbol <file>:<line>) to pick one.

Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                            Symbol to analyze (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>             Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>             Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --depth 1|2               Caller-traversal depth (default: 2)
  --limit <n>               Max entries per section (default: 15)
  --format text|json        Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Total text budget (default: 4096)
  --exclude-tests           Drop test-only entries
  --head                    Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth (default: full)

    20	types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
    21	agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

    23	## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)
    24	
    25	Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:
    26	
    27	    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"
    28	
    29	Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
    30	line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
    31	edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.
    32	
    33	## Hard rules
    34	
    35	1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
    36	2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
    37	   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
    38	3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
    39	       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
    40	4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
    41	5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
    42	   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
    43	6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
    44	7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
    45	       entire graph capabilities --json
    46	
    47	## When NOT to use the graph
    48	
    49	If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
    50	by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.
    51	
    52	## Reference
    53	
    54	    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    55	    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    56	    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    57	    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    58	    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    59	    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

    62	// agentPointerBegin/End delimit the block init-agents manages inside AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md,
    63	// so re-runs update in place instead of appending duplicates.

    65		agentPointerBegin = "<!-- entire-graph:begin -->"
    66		agentPointerEnd   = "<!-- entire-graph:end -->"
    67	)

    70		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("agent-guide", flag.ContinueOnError)
    71		fs.SetOutput(opts.Stderr)

    73			return err
    74		}
    75		fmt.Fprint(opts.Stdout, agentGuide)

    77	}

    81	// marker-guarded pointer block into AGENTS.md (the cross-agent convention) and CLAUDE.md
    82	// (which additionally understands the @-import line).
    83	func runInitAgents(opts Options, args []string) error {

    89		}

    92			return err
    93		}

    96		}

    98		guidePath := filepath.Join(root, ".entire", "graph-agent.md")
    99		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(guidePath), 0o755); err != nil {
   100			return err
   101		}
   102		if err := os.WriteFile(guidePath, []byte(agentGuide), 0o644); err != nil {
   103			return err
   104		}
   105		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "wrote %s\n", guidePath)
   106	
   107		pointer := agentPointerBegin + "\n" +
   108			"This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with\n" +
   109			"grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance\n" +
   110			"for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification.\n" +
   111			"@.entire/graph-agent.md\n" +
   112			agentPointerEnd + "\n"
   113	
   114		for _, name := range []string{"AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"} {
   115			path := filepath.Join(root, name)
   116			if err := upsertPointerBlock(path, pointer); err != nil {
   117				return fmt.Errorf("init-agents: %s: %w", name, err)
   118			}
   119			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "updated %s\n", path)
   120		}
   121		return nil
   122	}

   125	// existing marker-delimited block in place, so repeated runs never duplicate content.
   126	func upsertPointerBlock(path, block string) error {
   127		existing, err := os.ReadFile(path)
   128		if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   129			return err
   130		}
   131		content := string(existing)
   132		begin := strings.Index(content, agentPointerBegin)
   133		end := strings.Index(content, agentPointerEnd)
   134		switch {
   135		case begin >= 0 && end > begin:
   136			content = content[:begin] + strings.TrimSuffix(block, "\n") + content[end+len(agentPointerEnd):]
   137		case len(content) == 0:
   138			content = block
   139		default:
   140			if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
   141				content += "\n"
   142			}
   143			content += "\n" + block
   144		}
   145		return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644)
   146	}

     7		"path/filepath"
     8		"strings"
     9	)
    10	
    11	// agentGuide is the canonical, agent-agnostic operating guide for coding agents using the
    12	// graph in a CONSUMING project (not this repo). It ships inside the binary so every install
    13	// carries the current doctrine; `init-agents` distributes it into a project's AGENTS.md /
    14	// CLAUDE.md via a small pointer block, and `agent-guide` prints it for any agent or human.
    15	// It is resolution-first: graph retrieval narrows exploration, but source inspection and
    16	// focused verification remain required before an agent declares the task complete.
    17	const agentGuide = `# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)
    18	
    19	You have a deterministic local code graph: ` + "`entire graph`" + ` (functions, classes, methods,
    20	types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
    21	agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.
    22	
    23	## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)
    24	
    25	Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:
    26	
    27	    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"
    28	
    29	Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
    30	line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
    31	edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.
    32	
    33	## Hard rules
    34	
    35	1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
    36	2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
    37	   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
    38	3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
    39	       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
    40	4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
    41	5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
    42	   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
    43	6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
    44	7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
    45	       entire graph capabilities --json
    46	
    47	## When NOT to use the graph
    48	
    49	If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
    50	by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.
    51	
    52	## Reference
    53	
    54	    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    55	    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    56	    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    57	    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    58	    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    59	    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)
    60	`
    61	
    62	// agentPointerBegin/End delimit the block init-agents manages inside AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md,
    63	// so re-runs update in place instead of appending duplicates.
    64	const (
    65		agentPointerBegin = "<!-- entire-graph:begin -->"
    66		agentPointerEnd   = "<!-- entire-graph:end -->"
    67	)
    68	
    69	func runAgentGuide(opts Options, args []string) error {
    70		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("agent-guide", flag.ContinueOnError)
    71		fs.SetOutput(opts.Stderr)
    72		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
    73			return err
    74		}
    75		fmt.Fprint(opts.Stdout, agentGuide)
    76		return nil
    77	}
    78	
    79	// runInitAgents installs the guide into a consuming project so ANY coding agent finds it:
    80	// writes .entire/graph-agent.md (plugin-managed, overwritten on re-run) and upserts a
    81	// marker-guarded pointer block into AGENTS.md (the cross-agent convention) and CLAUDE.md
    82	// (which additionally understands the @-import line).
    83	func runInitAgents(opts Options, args []string) error {
    84		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("init-agents", flag.ContinueOnError)
    85		fs.SetOutput(opts.Stderr)
    86		repo := fs.String("repo", ".", "project root to install the agent guide into")
    87		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
    88			return err
    89		}
    90		root, err := filepath.Abs(*repo)
    91		if err != nil {
    92			return err
    93		}
    94		if info, err := os.Stat(root); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
    95			return fmt.Errorf("init-agents: %s is not a directory", root)
    96		}
    97	
    98		guidePath := filepath.Join(root, ".entire", "graph-agent.md")
    99		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(guidePath), 0o755); err != nil {
   100			return err
   101		}
   102		if err := os.WriteFile(guidePath, []byte(agentGuide), 0o644); err != nil {
   103			return err
   104		}
   105		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "wrote %s\n", guidePath)
   106	
   107		pointer := agentPointerBegin + "\n" +
   108			"This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with\n" +
   109			"grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance\n" +
   110			"for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification.\n" +
   111			"@.entire/graph-agent.md\n" +
   112			agentPointerEnd + "\n"
   113	
   114		for _, name := range []string{"AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"} {
   115			path := filepath.Join(root, name)
   116			if err := upsertPointerBlock(path, pointer); err != nil {
   117				return fmt.Errorf("init-agents: %s: %w", name, err)
   118			}
   119			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stdout, "updated %s\n", path)
   120		}
   121		return nil
   122	}
   123	
   124	// upsertPointerBlock appends the block to path (creating the file if absent), or replaces the
   125	// existing marker-delimited block in place, so repeated runs never duplicate content.
   126	func upsertPointerBlock(path, block string) error {
   127		existing, err := os.ReadFile(path)
   128		if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   129			return err
   130		}
   131		content := string(existing)
   132		begin := strings.Index(content, agentPointerBegin)
   133		end := strings.Index(content, agentPointerEnd)
   134		switch {
   135		case begin >= 0 && end > begin:
   136			content = content[:begin] + strings.TrimSuffix(block, "\n") + content[end+len(agentPointerEnd):]
   137		case len(content) == 0:
   138			content = block
   139		default:
   140			if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") {
   141				content += "\n"
   142			}
   143			content += "\n" + block
   144		}
   145		return os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o644)
   146	}

1	# Operations
     2	
     3	`entire-graph` is a local Entire CLI plugin. The operational surface is intentionally
     4	small: build the provider, install the local executable into Entire's plugin
     5	directory, and generate checksum-backed release archives.
     6	
     7	## Requirements
     8	
     9	- The Entire CLI and Git must be on `PATH` for local installation.
    10	- Development uses Go 1.26. Tree-sitter bindings require CGO and a working C
    11	  compiler for the target platform.
    12	- Release archives require `tar` and `shasum`. Signing additionally requires
    13	  either `cosign` or `gpg` and a configured local key.
    14	
    15	## Local Install
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	scripts/install-local.sh
    19	```
    20	
    21	The script builds `./entire-graph`, installs it with `entire plugin install
    22	./entire-graph --force`, and prints `entire graph version`. It fails before writing
    23	anything if the parent `entire` CLI is not on `PATH`.
    24	
    25	## Release Archives
    26	
    27	```sh
    28	scripts/release.sh
    29	```
    30	
    31	The release script writes `dist/release-<version>/` with one `.tar.gz` archive per
    32	target and a `SHA256SUMS` manifest. `VERSION=<value>` overrides the version;
    33	otherwise the script uses `git describe --tags --always --dirty`.
    34	
    35	By default the script builds the current host target. Set `ENTIRE_RELEASE_TARGETS`
    36	to a space-separated list of `GOOS/GOARCH` targets to request more builds:
    37	
    38	```sh
    39	ENTIRE_RELEASE_TARGETS="darwin/arm64 linux/amd64" scripts/release.sh
    40	```
    41	
    42	`entire-graph` includes native tree-sitter parser bindings, so cross-platform
    43	artifacts require the matching cgo-capable compiler/toolchain for each requested
    44	target. The script records checksums for artifacts it successfully builds; it
    45	also signs archives when a local signing key is explicitly configured:
    46	
    47	- `COSIGN_KEY=<key-ref>` with `cosign` on `PATH` writes `<archive>.sig`.
    48	- `GPG_SIGNING_KEY=<key-id>` with `gpg` on `PATH` writes `<archive>.asc`.
    49	
    50	If both signing variables are set and both tools are available, cosign takes
    51	precedence and the script writes only the `.sig` file.
    52	
    53	The script does not publish artifacts.

1	# Entire Brain and Entire Graph boundaries
     2	
     3	entire-graph is a **provider**: it turns a repository revision or working tree into a typed,
     4	no-egress snapshot and answers ranked queries over it. Entire Brain is the **consumer**: it ingests
     5	that snapshot alongside durable facts, sessions and checkpoints, and is where knowledge that is
     6	not reproducible from repository state belongs.
     7	
     8	The line is not organizational; it is a property of the artifact. Facts derived from one requested
     9	repository state belong here, including explicitly labeled co-change relations from bounded Git
    10	history anchored at a revision. State accumulated across repositories, users, or independent runs
    11	belongs to Brain. Hidden provider state would make identical requests produce different results and
    12	weaken every downstream claim built on them.
    13	
    14	This file exists so the items below are not re-litigated each time a competitor ships one.
    15	
    16	## The verdicts
    17	
    18	### MCP server surface — **Brain's job**
    19	An MCP surface adds client-facing tool, lifecycle, and policy decisions that are not graph facts.
    20	Entire Brain already owns that integration. The provider stays a one-shot, no-egress binary whose
    21	output is a stable NDJSON contract. Direct provider calls remain shell-outs; Entire Brain supplies
    22	the local MCP tool surface for clients that need one. That boundary is intentional, not a reason
    23	to grow a second server in this repository.
    24	
    25	### Multi-repo / cross-project graph — **Brain's job**
    26	`repoKey` is per-repository and every command takes one `--repo` on purpose. Committed-tree cache
    27	identity includes the repository, checkout, tree, profile, limits, selected files, and ignore
    28	inputs; there is no equivalent identity for "nine repositories as of roughly now." A merged
    29	cross-project graph is inherently a continuously reconciled store — Brain's shape, not a
    30	provider's. The provider's contribution is that its snapshots are cheap to ingest and its symbol
    31	IDs are stable, so N of them can be merged upstream.
    32	
    33	### save-result / reflect feedback loop — **Brain's job**
    34	A feedback loop is memory: outcomes recorded per user over time, decayed, corroborated, and fed
    35	back as a ranking overlay. Landing that here would make search results depend on who ran it and
    36	what they clicked last week — the exact opposite of the determinism the schema contract and every
    37	benchmark claim rest on. Brain is the correct home precisely because it is allowed to be stateful.
    38	If a learned overlay ever influences provider ranking, it must arrive as an explicit input to a
    39	query, never as hidden local state.
    40	
    41	### Human dashboards beyond a markdown report — **neither / not worth it**
    42	`index --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` is now in the provider, and it is the right amount: a
    43	deterministic, diffable, committable projection of a snapshot the tool already has in memory, which
    44	lets a human judge the tool in thirty seconds. An interactive HTML force-graph is not that. It is a
    45	UI product with its own rendering and performance envelope, it is unusable at the node counts this
    46	graph reaches on a real monorepo, and Brain's web surfaces are where an Entire user is already
    47	looking at their code. Building one here would be the most visible and least useful thing in this
    48	document.
    49	
    50	### Per-file incremental invalidation — **graph's job, not done yet**
    51	Tree-hash keying means a one-character commit pays a full rebuild. That is a provider concern
    52	(cache correctness and reuse of repository-derived facts) and it is the highest-value unbuilt item
    53	on this side of the line. It is unbuilt, not declined.
    54	
    55	### Watch mode / daemon — **neither / not worth it**
    56	Explicitly declined, and the reasoning holds: re-running `index` *is* the refresh, a changed tree
    57	misses the cache by construction, and a daemon would add an authoritative mutable process where
    58	the provider currently has only rebuildable derivative caches.
    59	
    60	### Named per-host installers — **graph's job, not done yet**
    61	`init-agents` writing `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` already covers the instruction-file hosts implicitly.
    62	Per-host installers are cheap, additive, and a real distribution win; they are simply not
    63	architecture, so they queue behind product behavior.
    64	
    65	## One-line test for anything new
    66	
    67	Would this make two identical requests differ, or require mutable state that outlives one command?
    68	If yes, it is Brain's. If no, it is arguably ours — and then the only question is priority.

     2	
     3	Status: Accepted
     4	Date: 2026-07-28
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	`entire-graph` has two committed-tree caches of the same shape:
     9	
    10	| cache | key | consumers | on by default? |
    11	|---|---|---|---|
    12	| search snapshot (`internal/sem/search_cache.go`, `searchSnapshotKey`) | `<cacheDir>/search/…/<sha256>.json.gz` | `search`, `neighbors`, `impact`, `index` | no — `searchFlags{Worktree: true}`, so only `--head` |
    13	| provider records (`internal/sem/records_cache.go`, `providerRecordsKey`) | `<cacheDir>/records/…/<sha256>.json.gz` | whole-graph `snapshot`, `symbols`, `edges` | yes — those commands default to committed-tree |
    14	
    15	`cacheDir` is `--cache-dir` else `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`: one flat global directory, shared by
    16	every repository and every worktree on the machine.
    17	
    18	The question this ADR answers: with N worktrees off one repository — branch A refactoring a
    19	package, branch B renaming symbols, `main` moving on — can a cache entry written on one branch
    20	be served on another, and what does the current keying cost?
    21	
    22	Both keys hash the cache version, the **checkout path** (`filepath.Abs(repo)`), the provider
    23	version, the **HEAD tree hash**, the profile, `MaxParseBytes`, `OnlyFiles`, and the **contents**
    24	of any `--ignore-file` / `--include-file`. In `--head` mode the file set is otherwise a pure
    25	function of the tree: `openSource` lists via `gitutil.ListFiles(ctx, repo, committedRevision)`
    26	and filters with `loadExplicitIgnoreMatcher` (content-hashed) plus a tree-derived
    27	`headIgnoreMatcher`. `.git/info/exclude` and `core.excludesFile` reach only the working-tree
    28	path, which is never cached.
    29	
    30	Measured on a binary built from `cdcb8db`, against an isolated clone with three linked
    31	worktrees — `wtA`/`wtC` at `cdcb8db`, `wtB` at `6e4bfde`, 3 of 317 tracked files differing:
    32	
    33	**Branch drift is already safe.** The tree hash is in both keys, so switching branches at one
    34	checkout path misses:
    35	
    36	```
    37	symbols at cdcb8db = 5740 ; at 6e4bfde = 5736
    38	byte-identical?    = no          cache entries = 2
    39	```
    40	
    41	Two worktrees cannot collide either, because the checkout path is in the key.
    42	
    43	**But two inputs that do shape the graph are not in either key, and both produce a silent wrong
    44	answer.** First, the file-listing cap: `capSourceFiles` truncates to
    45	`resolveMaxSourceFiles(options.MaxFiles)`, which folds in `ENTIRE_GRAPH_MAX_FILES`. Neither the
    46	option nor the effective cap is keyed or re-validated:
    47	
    48	```
    49	1. cap=5, cold  -> symbols = 28     entries=1
    50	2. NO cap, warm -> symbols = 28     entries=1   <== WRONG
    51	3. NO cap, cold -> symbols = 5740               <== correct
    52	```
    53	
    54	99.5% of the graph absent, carrying a `W_FILE_LIMIT` warning into a run that asked for no cap.
    55	One `entire-brain` ingest with a bound poisons every later unbounded query on that tree.
    56	
    57	Second, repository identity: `repoKey` resolves the GitHub remote, and **every** symbol and file
    58	ID is `repoKey + ":" + …`. It is not keyed and not validated on a direct hit:
    59	
    60	```
    61	1. remote=entireio/entire-graph, cold -> repo_key=gh/entireio/entire-graph   id=gh/entireio/entire-graph:JSON:…
    62	2. remote=someoneelse/a-fork,    warm -> repo_key=gh/entireio/entire-graph   id=gh/entireio/entire-graph:JSON:…  <== WRONG
    63	3. remote=someoneelse/a-fork,    cold -> repo_key=gh/someoneelse/a-fork      id=gh/someoneelse/a-fork:JSON:…     <== correct
    64	```
    65	
    66	`selectiveSearchSnapshotFromFull` already rejects a `RepoKey` mismatch, which shows the
    67	invariant is known; the two direct-hit paths and all of `records_cache.go` skip the check.
    68	
    69	**And keying on the checkout path costs everything the tree hash was supposed to buy.** One
    70	shared cache dir, three worktrees, two of them at a byte-identical tree:
    71	
    72	```
    73	### A. DEFAULT MODE (working tree; no --head)
    74	wtA default run1     0.06s  entries=0   cache=0K
    75	wtA default run2     0.04s  entries=0   cache=0K
    76	
    77	### B. --head MODE, ONE shared cache dir
    78	wtA --head cold      9.02s  entries=1   cache=428K
    79	wtA --head warm      0.87s  entries=1   cache=428K
    80	wtB --head cold      9.37s  entries=2   cache=856K
    81	wtB --head warm      1.07s  entries=2   cache=856K
    82	
    83	### C. wtC = THIRD worktree at the SAME COMMIT/TREE as wtA
    84	wtC --head           9.04s  entries=3   cache=1284K
    85	```
    86	
    87	The cache is worth having (9.02s → 0.87s, **10.4×**). But `wtB`, differing in 3 of 317 files,
    88	pays a full rebuild and a second full 428 KB entry; and `wtC`, whose graph is **byte-identical**
    89	to `wtA`'s, still pays a full 9.04s build and a third 435 KB entry. N worktrees at one commit
    90	cost N × 9s and N × 435 KB where 1 × would do.
    91	
    92	## Decision
    93	
    94	**The cache key becomes a total function of every input that shapes the graph: repository
    95	identity + tree + all snapshot-shaping options. Nothing that can change the output is left
    96	implicit, and every discriminating field is re-validated on load.**
    97	
    98	Concretely, in both `searchSnapshotKey` and `providerRecordsKey`, and in both on-disk
    99	envelopes and their `valid…` predicates:
   100	
   101	1. **Repository identity (`repoKey`) joins the key** and is compared on load. Identity is what
   102	   every symbol ID embeds, so an entry built under a different identity must miss, not be
   103	   re-served. This replaces the checkout path as the *identity* term — the path is a proxy for
   104	   identity that is simultaneously too strict (three worktrees, one graph, three entries) and
   105	   too loose (identity can change under a fixed path).
   106	2. **The effective file-listing cap joins the key** — `resolveMaxSourceFiles(options.MaxFiles)`,
   107	   the resolved value, so `ENTIRE_GRAPH_MAX_FILES` is covered by the same term as the option.
   108	3. **Cache version strings bump** (`search-snapshot-v5`, `provider-records-v2`) so entries
   109	   written by the old keying are unreachable by name rather than merely unfindable by hash.
   110	
   111	**The trade-off accepted: this only adds misses, never hits.** Every change above narrows what
   112	counts as a valid entry. Runs that previously reused an entry across a remote-URL change or a
   113	cap change now rebuild — correctly. We accept the extra cold builds and one extra `git remote`
   114	subprocess per cache lookup, because a wrong cache hit is worse than a slow miss. We do not
   115	take the sharing win in the same change, so no new reuse surface is opened alongside a
   116	correctness fix.
   117	
   118	## Consequences
   119	
   120	**What this does NOT do — explicitly:**
   121	
   122	- **No cross-worktree sharing.** The checkout path stays in the key, so `wtC` still rebuilds
   123	  `wtA`'s identical graph and the third 435 KB entry is still written. Keying on identity alone
   124	  is now *possible* (identity is in the key and validated), but not *safe* yet: on a cache hit
   125	  `search.go:356` overwrites the response's `repoRoot` from the cached header, so a shared entry
   126	  would report the wrong checkout path — and `records_cache.go` stores opaque NDJSON bytes, so
   127	  restamping its header means rewriting the serialized first line. Both are separate changes
   128	  with their own tests.
   129	- **No per-file content-hash caching / incrementality.** The prize measured above — `wtB`
   130	  differing in 3 of 317 files should reuse ~99% of the parse, not 0% — needs a per-blob parse
   131	  cache keyed by blob hash plus relation re-resolution over the union, which is a new index
   132	  layer, not a key change. This ADR is its prerequisite: a per-blob cache is only sharable
   133	  across worktrees if repository identity is a keyed, validated term, which it now is.
   134	- **No change to working-tree mode.** It stays uncached; dirty state has no durable key. The
   135	  0-entry rows in the measurement are that policy, not a write failure.
   136	- **No change to tree-only keying of the parsed graph.** Two commits sharing a tree still share
   137	  an entry, and `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` co-change edges are still allowed to come from the other
   138	  commit's history — already documented on `searchSnapshotKey` and unchanged here.
   139	- **No fix for the linked-worktree `.git/info/exclude` ENOTDIR failure** seen while measuring
   140	  (`read ignore file ".../wtA/.git/info/exclude": not a directory`, exit 1). That is
   141	  working-tree-only, therefore cache-irrelevant, and is owned by a separate change.
   142	
   143	**What it costs:** every existing cache entry is orphaned on disk under the old version
   144	directory; the first run after upgrading is cold. One additional `git remote` invocation per
   145	committed-tree cache lookup, alongside the two `rev-parse` calls already made.
   146	
   147	**What it buys:** the two measured silent-wrong-answer paths become misses, and the key is now
   148	defensible as complete — the audit above enumerates the committed-tree inputs, and after this
   149	change each one is either hashed or provably tree-derived.
   150	
   151	**Verified on the same three-worktree lab, with a binary built from this change.** Both holes
   152	close and nothing else moves:
   153	
   154	```
   155	HOLE 1  NO cap, warm -> symbols = 5740  entries=2   (was 28, entries=1)
   156	HOLE 2  remote re-pointed, warm -> repo_key=gh/someoneelse/a-fork   (was gh/entireio/entire-graph)
   157	branch switch at one path -> 2 entries, 5740 vs 5736 symbols   (unchanged)
   158	wtA --head cold 9.75s -> warm 0.86s                            (warm win unchanged, 11.3x)
   159	wtC --head at wtA's identical tree -> still a full build, third entry   (unchanged, by design)
   160	```
   161

   163

   165	independently keyed `searchSnapshotKey` on repository identity and bumped that cache to
   166	`search-snapshot-v6`, so the identity half of the problem was already solved **for the search
   167	cache**. Two gaps remained and are what this change actually closes:
   168	
   169	- `searchSnapshotKey` did not fold in the resolved file cap. Bumped to `search-snapshot-v7`.
   170	- `providerRecordsKey` folded in NEITHER identity NOR the cap, and it is the cache that is on by
   171	  default. Bumped to `provider-records-v2`; `LoadProviderRecords`/`StoreProviderRecords` now take a
   172	  `context.Context` so the key can include `repoKey(ctx, repo)` the way the search cache does.
   173	
   174	Still explicitly NOT done, unchanged from the original decision: cross-worktree sharing (blocked by
   175	`repoRoot` being overwritten from the cached header) and per-file content-hash incrementality, for
   176	which a total key is the prerequisite.

     1	# Entire Brain and Entire Graph boundaries
     2	
     3	entire-graph is a **provider**: it turns a repository revision or working tree into a typed,
     4	no-egress snapshot and answers ranked queries over it. Entire Brain is the **consumer**: it ingests
     5	that snapshot alongside durable facts, sessions and checkpoints, and is where knowledge that is
     6	not reproducible from repository state belongs.
     7	
     8	The line is not organizational; it is a property of the artifact. Facts derived from one requested
     9	repository state belong here, including explicitly labeled co-change relations from bounded Git
    10	history anchored at a revision. State accumulated across repositories, users, or independent runs
    11	belongs to Brain. Hidden provider state would make identical requests produce different results and
    12	weaken every downstream claim built on them.
    13	
    14	This file exists so the items below are not re-litigated each time a competitor ships one.
    15	
    16	## The verdicts
    17	
    18	### MCP server surface — **Brain's job**
    19	An MCP surface adds client-facing tool, lifecycle, and policy decisions that are not graph facts.
    20	Entire Brain already owns that integration. The provider stays a one-shot, no-egress binary whose
    21	output is a stable NDJSON contract. Direct provider calls remain shell-outs; Entire Brain supplies
    22	the local MCP tool surface for clients that need one. That boundary is intentional, not a reason
    23	to grow a second server in this repository.
    24	
    25	### Multi-repo / cross-project graph — **Brain's job**
    26	`repoKey` is per-repository and every command takes one `--repo` on purpose. Committed-tree cache
    27	identity includes the repository, checkout, tree, profile, limits, selected files, and ignore
    28	inputs; there is no equivalent identity for "nine repositories as of roughly now." A merged
    29	cross-project graph is inherently a continuously reconciled store — Brain's shape, not a
    30	provider's. The provider's contribution is that its snapshots are cheap to ingest and its symbol
    31	IDs are stable, so N of them can be merged upstream.
    32	
    33	### save-result / reflect feedback loop — **Brain's job**
    34	A feedback loop is memory: outcomes recorded per user over time, decayed, corroborated, and fed
    35	back as a ranking overlay. Landing that here would make search results depend on who ran it and
    36	what they clicked last week — the exact opposite of the determinism the schema contract and every
    37	benchmark claim rest on. Brain is the correct home precisely because it is allowed to be stateful.
    38	If a learned overlay ever influences provider ranking, it must arrive as an explicit input to a
    39	query, never as hidden local state.

    42	`index --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` is now in the provider, and it is the right amount: a
    43	deterministic, diffable, committable projection of a snapshot the tool already has in memory, which

 # Entire Graph
 
 **This release is for your agents.**
 
 Entire Graph gives coding agents a precomputed, deterministic map of your codebase — every
 function, type, route, and call relationship — so they can start from ranked
 structural evidence instead of broad grep-and-read exploration. It is 100% local:
 no network, no model calls, no keys.

 ```
 
 Then, in any repo your agents work in:

 entire graph init-agents
 ```

 ## Evidence status
 
 The former 54.9% Haiku, 57.7% Sonnet, and 31–73% open-model token-savings
 figures are withdrawn. They were token-first measurements under a prompt policy
 that encouraged the graph arms to stop early and did not require equivalent
 resolution evidence from every arm. “Patch produced” was also reported as task
 completion, which is not the same as passing the task's tests.

 entire graph snapshot-query --input graph.compact.ndjson --from '<stable-id>' --relation CALLS --format ndjson
